questions.q: What do Livingston's interviews suggest matters most when launching a company?
a: A talented, flexible team
A detailed business plan
A large funding round
A patented technology
questions.why: The first lesson says the founders of Excite succeeded because of their team, not because they had a clear plan.

questions.q: What did the Excite founders have before they settled on a business?
a: A group of passionate, intelligent friends and a goal
A finished product and paying customers
A patent and a team of lawyers
A five-year plan and a signed lease
questions.why: The summary says Kraus and five Stanford friends knew only that they were capable and wanted to build something useful.

questions.q: Why did Joel Spolsky aim to run Fog Creek without investor capital?
a: He wanted to keep the workplace he had designed
He could not find anyone willing to invest
He planned to sell the company quickly
He wanted to avoid paying taxes on profits
questions.why: The second lesson says investors would have seen his offices, flights and vacations as wasteful frills.

questions.q: What happened when Fog Creek raised its price from $199 to $999?
a: Customers saw more value and bought more units
Sales collapsed until the price was lowered again
Customers demanded longer money-back guarantees
The company had to hire extra support staff
questions.why: The second lesson uses the price rise to show how avoiding investors forced a smarter business model.

questions.q: What was the most common advice Livingston heard from the founders she interviewed?
a: Listen closely to what your customers want
Hire only managers with years of experience
Launch as quietly as you possibly can
Copy whatever your competitors do well
questions.why: The third lesson says listening to customers is how founders create something of real value.
